> id="main-content" is used more than once

| | |

| Rule | `REACT_029` |
| Severity | 🟡 warning |

### 💡 How to fix

Make ids unique; label and aria-* references resolve to the first match only

### 🤖 AI review (4)

> Written by a language model against the surrounding code. The finding itself is rule-based and reproducible; these suggestions are not — review before applying.

**dashboard/components/Dashboard.tsx:380** · confidence 90%

The id 'main-content' is applied to three separate <main> elements (loading, error, and success states). Since only one is rendered at a time, this is technically valid, but it is poor practice that can confuse assistive technologies if the component re-renders or if the id is referenced by external scripts. It is safer to use a unique id or remove it if not strictly required for navigation.

**dashboard/components/Dashboard.tsx:469** · confidence 100%

The id 'main-content' is applied to three separate <main> elements (loading, error, and success states). Since only one is rendered at a time, the duplicate ID is technically harmless for DOM uniqueness, but it violates the rule that IDs must be unique within the document and can confuse assistive technologies if the DOM structure changes or if multiple instances are ever rendered simultaneously.

```tsx
Remove the id="main-content" attribute from all three <main> elements. If a skip-link target is needed, add id="main-content" to only the primary success-state <main> element and ensure the loading/error states do not use it.
```

**components/Dashboard.tsx:380** · confidence 90%

The id 'main-content' is applied to three separate <main> elements (loading, error, and success states). Since only one is rendered at a time, this is technically valid, but the static analyser flags it as a duplicate. For screen reader users, having multiple potential landmarks with the same ID can cause confusion if the page structure changes or if the analyser assumes all are present.

**components/Dashboard.tsx:469** · confidence 100%

The id 'main-content' is assigned to the <main> element in three separate conditional return paths (loading, error, and success states). This creates duplicate IDs in the DOM when the component re-renders or if any structure changes, causing screen readers and assistive technologies to fail to uniquely identify the primary content landmark.

```tsx
<main
                id="main-content"
                tabIndex={-1}
                style={{
                    display: 'flex',
                    alignItems: 'center',
                    gap: '0.75rem',
                    padding: '2rem',
                    fontFamily: 'monospace',
                    outline: 'none',
                }}
            >
```
